title: Connect-volume seed: prioritize device-reported / last-known volume over fixed default
why: Alec (2026-07-29): the connect seed today always uses a fixed connect-default (35%) on a user-initiated connect, a holdover from when the seed inherited the Macs system volume and could blast the user. He wants the priority reordered: (1) the device/system own reported current volume if available, (2) otherwise the level that device previously had in our system, persisted per device across restarts, (3) the fixed connect-default only as a last resort for a never-seen device. Only the user-connect branch changes; F-REBIND (out-of-band reconnect) already preserves the in-session level and is untouched.
what: Read-only research + plan: docs/plans/PLAN-CONNECT-VOLUME-SEED.md. Traces the current seed (NativeBackend.connectVolumeSeed, userConnectSeed, stashedVolume, known[id].volume), the wire/UI domain conversion setSpeakerVolume already demonstrates for a receiver-reported level, and the vendored AirPlay sender/receiver protocol. Feasibility verdict: no GET_PARAMETER or any pull primitive exists anywhere in the vendored C sender (0 matches); the sender is the protocols volume authority and only ever pushes SET_PARAMETER. The only receiver-volume signal is an asynchronous, receiver-initiated push (RTSP reverse /event channel or DACP setproperty, both already wired to NativeBackend), coded and documented as a change notification, not an initial-state announcement; whether any receiver fires one unprompted at connect time, early enough to beat the seeds own push, is unverified and needs a live hardware probe (T-I1). Persistence finding: known[id].volume and stashedVolume are in-memory only today, nothing is written to disk, so tier 2 (persisted last-known level) is new work, not a rename -- DeviceIconStore.swift is the direct pattern to copy (stable colon-hex device id, Codable versioned JSON, same Application Support directory). Also raises, without deciding, an anti-blast open question: a device reporting 100% reopens the exact blast risk the fixed default was built to close, so the plan proposes T-I2 as an owner decision between trusting tier 1 unclamped, a cheap ceiling clamp, or a genuine ramp. Task list separates investigation-remaining (T-I1 live protocol probe, T-I2 anti-blast decision) from implementation (T-F1 bounded-listen tier-1 mechanism, T-F2 DeviceVolumeStore, T-F3 write-through wiring, T-F4 rewire connectVolumeSeed, T-F5 tests, T-F6 docs), gated on the two owner decisions.

title: Per-app tap make-before-break on default-device change
why: Live repro 2026-08-05 (sid E41C6D0A, ~21:08:30Z): switching the Mac default output (MacBook Pro Speakers <-> AirPods Max, both 48000) pauses the per-app AirPlay route (Spotify) ~1s while the Mac own audio switches seamlessly. Telemetry shows the capture hole: device_change_fired 30.669 -> aggregate_destroy 30.694 -> aggregate_create 30.809 -> capturing 30.830 (~160ms of zero buffers), which the AirPlay receiver renders as the ~1s audible gap. WWDC25 session 260 is explicit: intents appear in Spotlight on Mac automatically, WITHOUT an AppShortcutsProvider, provided (a) the parameter summary contains all required parameters that have no default value, (b) the intent is not hidden (isDiscoverable false / assistantOnly true), and (c) it has a perform method. (2) NEW HARD REQUIREMENT: every intent needs a ParameterSummary listing all required parameters with no default, or the action silently vanishes from Spotlight. This bites the auto-start volume parameter directly - it is deliberately REQUIRED (no default), so it must appear in the summary; same for the speaker on Set Speaker Volume. Treat ParameterSummary as mandatory on every intent, not polish. Entity indexing (IndexedEntity + donation) stays a separate optional add that would make individual speakers findable in Spotlight - not needed for any of the six verbs.

title: Profiles/scenes: snapshot the current setup and recall it by name
why: The step past saved groups. Sonos users have begged for volume-snapshot scenes for years and Sonos never shipped it; SoundSource 6 just did, as 'Quick Configs'. Audiouter's saved groups already snapshot per-device volumes, so this extends persistence machinery that exists rather than inventing any.
what: SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-07 once 035 (App Intents) was scoped. Split this into its two halves and build only the second. REPLAY - apply a named set of devices, volumes and routes - is delivered for free by 035: with the per-speaker verbs in Shortcuts a user hand-authors 'kitchen 30, living room 40, activate Movie Night' with no app support at all. Do not build an in-app replay UI that duplicates it. SNAPSHOT is what remains and is the actual feature: one action that captures the CURRENT live state - selected devices, each device's volume and mute, Main level, per-app routes, and later per-device trim (033) and EQ (034) - stores it under a name, and recalls it. The value is that the user never has to author or maintain the list; they get the setup they are already listening to. Extends the persistence pattern saved groups already use (GroupStore snapshots per-device volumes today). The real cost is apply-time edge cases - missing devices, apps that are not running, conflicts with the currently active state - so the silent-fallback rules need designing up front. Optional follow-on: expose the recall as an App Intent too, so a snapshot becomes usable inside a Shortcut.

title: Per-speaker auto-connect on appearance
why: TuneBlade's set-and-forget shape (per-receiver auto-connect plus force-reconnect) is what turns a session tool into always-on whole-home infrastructure. title: Codec transparency: surface that the wire is lossless ALAC
